_about: Planedex catalog. Species are ICAO aircraft type codes. types: jet, regional, heavy, jumbo, bizjet, turboprop, prop, rotor, military, fire. rarity: 1 Common, 2 Uncommon, 3 Rare, 4 Epic, 5 Legendary. A type code the receiver catches that isn't listed here still counts; planedex_push.py prints it so it can be added.

A319.name: Airbus A319
A319.fact: A shorter A320, built for smaller routes.

A320.name: Airbus A320
A320.fact: The first airliner with digital fly-by-wire controls.

A20N.name: Airbus A320neo
A20N.fact: An A320 with new, bigger, quieter engines.

A321.name: Airbus A321
A321.fact: The longest member of the original A320 family.

A21N.name: Airbus A321neo
A21N.fact: "neo" stands for New Engine Option: bigger, quieter engines.

BCS1.name: Airbus A220-100
BCS1.fact: The smaller A220, designed in Canada as the Bombardier CSeries.

BCS3.name: Airbus A220-300
BCS3.fact: Designed by Bombardier as the CSeries before Airbus took it over.

B738.name: Boeing 737-800
B738.fact: One of the most-built jetliners ever.

B739.name: Boeing 737-900
B739.fact: The longest of the Next-Generation 737s. Alaska flies lots of them.

B38M.name: Boeing 737 MAX 8
B38M.fact: Look for the zig-zag edges on the back of its engine covers.

B39M.name: Boeing 737 MAX 9
B39M.fact: A stretched MAX. Alaska and United fly lots of them.

B752.name: Boeing 757-200
B752.fact: A tall, skinny jet famous for its rocket-like climb.

B753.name: Boeing 757-300
B753.fact: The longest single-aisle twinjet ever built.

E75L.name: Embraer E175
E75L.fact: Horizon and SkyWest fly these all over the Northwest.

E75S.name: Embraer E175
E75S.fact: The short-wing version of the E175.

E190.name: Embraer E190
E190.fact: The middle size of Embraer's E-Jet family.

E195.name: Embraer E195
E195.fact: The biggest of Embraer's first-generation E-Jets.

E145.name: Embraer ERJ 145
E145.fact: A slim regional jet with its engines on the tail.

CRJ9.name: Bombardier CRJ900
CRJ9.fact: A stretched regional jet with tail-mounted engines.

CRJ7.name: Bombardier CRJ700
CRJ7.fact: A regional jet with tail-mounted engines and about 70 seats.

DH8D.name: De Havilland Dash 8-400
DH8D.fact: A fast, quiet turboprop airliner from Canada.

A333.name: Airbus A330-300
A333.fact: A twin-aisle workhorse that first flew in 1992.

A339.name: Airbus A330-900
A339.fact: The A330neo, with new engines and longer wings.

A359.name: Airbus A350-900
A359.fact: About half of it is made of carbon-fiber composites.

A35K.name: Airbus A350-1000
A35K.fact: The biggest A350, about 242 feet long.

B763.name: Boeing 767-300
B763.fact: Many now fly overnight packages for FedEx, UPS and Amazon.

B77L.name: Boeing 777-200LR / 777F
B77L.fact: The long-range 777. The freighter version hauls more than 100 tons.

B77W.name: Boeing 777-300ER
B77W.fact: Its GE90 engines were once the most powerful jet engines in the world.

B788.name: Boeing 787-8 Dreamliner
B788.fact: The first Dreamliner, made about half of carbon-fiber composites.

B789.name: Boeing 787-9 Dreamliner
B789.fact: Its big windows dim at the press of a button instead of using shades.

B78X.name: Boeing 787-10 Dreamliner
B78X.fact: The longest Dreamliner, built only in South Carolina.

B742.name: Boeing 747-200
B742.fact: An early jumbo with the short upper deck. Very few still fly.

B744.name: Boeing 747-400
B744.fact: The classic Queen of the Skies, hump and all. Many now fly as freighters.

B748.name: Boeing 747-8
B748.fact: The longest 747 ever, about 250 feet nose to tail.

A388.name: Airbus A380-800
A388.fact: The world's largest passenger airliner, with two full-length decks.

BLCF.name: Boeing 747 Dreamlifter
BLCF.fact: A puffed-up 747 that carries 787 parts between factories.

A124.name: Antonov An-124 Ruslan
A124.fact: A giant freighter that can carry trains and helicopters.

C25M.name: Cessna Citation M2
C25M.fact: An entry-level Citation jet that a single pilot can fly.

C25B.name: Cessna Citation CJ3
C25B.fact: A light business jet built to be flown by one pilot.

C25C.name: Cessna Citation CJ4
C25C.fact: The biggest and fastest of the CitationJet line.

C68A.name: Cessna Citation Latitude
C68A.fact: A midsize jet with a flat floor tall enough to stand up in.

CL35.name: Bombardier Challenger 350
CL35.fact: One of the best-selling business jets of its size.

CL60.name: Bombardier Challenger 600 series
CL60.fact: A wide-cabin business jet family that first flew in 1978.

F900.name: Dassault Falcon 900
F900.fact: A French business jet with three engines.

GLF5.name: Gulfstream V / G550
GLF5.fact: A long-range business jet. The military flies versions of it too.

GLEX.name: Bombardier Global Express / 6000
GLEX.fact: An ultra-long-range business jet that can cross an ocean nonstop.

GLF6.name: Gulfstream G650
GLF6.fact: One of the fastest business jets in the sky.

SF50.name: Cirrus Vision Jet
SF50.fact: A single-engine personal jet with a parachute for the whole plane.

PC24.name: Pilatus PC-24
PC24.fact: A business jet built to land on gravel runways.

PC12.name: Pilatus PC-12
PC12.fact: A Swiss single-engine turboprop. Life Flight uses them as air ambulances.

BE20.name: Beechcraft King Air 200
BE20.fact: A classic twin turboprop used for charters, cargo and air ambulances.

MU2.name: Mitsubishi MU-2
MU2.fact: A speedy Japanese twin turboprop with a high wing.

P46T.name: Piper M500
P46T.fact: A single-engine turboprop with a pressurized cabin.

C208.name: Cessna Caravan
C208.fact: A big single-engine turboprop that hauls packages to small towns.

C72R.name: Cessna 172RG Cutlass
C72R.fact: A Skyhawk cousin whose wheels fold up in flight.

C182.name: Cessna 182 Skylane
C182.fact: A bigger, more powerful cousin of the 172.

C185.name: Cessna 185 Skywagon
C185.fact: A tough bush plane with a tailwheel that can fly on wheels, floats or skis.

T206.name: Cessna Turbo Stationair
T206.fact: A rugged six-seater that hauls people and gear to backcountry strips.

P28R.name: Piper Arrow
P28R.fact: A four-seat Piper whose landing gear folds up.

M7.name: Maule M-7
M7.fact: A tough taildragger made for short, rough airstrips.

BE19.name: Beechcraft Sport
BE19.fact: A four-seat trainer from the Beechcraft Musketeer family.

AEST.name: Aerostar 600
AEST.fact: One of the fastest piston twins ever built.

SR22.name: Cirrus SR22
SR22.fact: The best-selling Cirrus, with a parachute for the whole airplane.

S22T.name: Cirrus SR22T
S22T.fact: A fast single that carries a parachute for the whole airplane.

B407.name: Bell 407
B407.fact: A four-blade helicopter. Life Flight Network flies them as air ambulances.

EC35.name: Airbus H135
EC35.fact: A twin-engine helicopter whose tail rotor hides inside a round fan.

R22.name: Robinson R22
R22.fact: A tiny two-seat helicopter, popular for training.

R44.name: Robinson R44
R44.fact: A four-seat helicopter, the R22's bigger sibling.

B212.name: Bell UH-1N Iroquois
B212.fact: The twin-engine version of the famous Huey helicopter.

C17.name: Boeing C-17 Globemaster III
C17.fact: The Air Force's big airlifter. It can land on short, rough runways.

P8.name: Boeing P-8 Poseidon
P8.fact: A Navy sub-hunter built from a Boeing 737.

K35R.name: Boeing KC-135 Stratotanker
K35R.fact: A flying gas station. Fairchild AFB, just west of Spokane, is home to a big fleet.

KC46.name: Boeing KC-46 Pegasus
KC46.fact: The Air Force's newest tanker, built from a Boeing 767.

C130.name: Lockheed C-130 Hercules
C130.fact: A four-engine military workhorse built since the 1950s.

V22.name: Bell Boeing V-22 Osprey
V22.fact: Takes off like a helicopter, then tilts its rotors to fly like a plane.

B52.name: Boeing B-52 Stratofortress
B52.fact: A giant eight-engine bomber that first flew in 1952.

VC25.name: Boeing VC-25A / E-4B
VC25.fact: Military 747s: Air Force One for the President, and the E-4B flying command posts.

CL2T.name: Canadair CL-415 Super Scooper
CL2T.fact: A water bomber that skims lakes to scoop up water for fires.

AT8T.name: Air Tractor AT-802
AT8T.fact: A big single-engine turboprop that fights wildfires and sprays crops.

B762.name: Boeing 767-200
B762.fact: The first and shortest 767. Most still flying carry cargo.

C180.name: Cessna 180 Skywagon
C180.fact: A rugged 1950s taildragger, the big brother of the Skywagon family.

COL4.name: Cessna 400 Corvalis
COL4.fact: One of the fastest single-engine piston planes ever built.

F2TH.name: Dassault Falcon 2000
F2TH.fact: A French twin-engine business jet with a roomy cabin.

K100.name: Kodiak 100
K100.fact: A tough bush plane built just up the road in Sandpoint, Idaho.

PA30.name: Piper Twin Comanche
PA30.fact: A sleek 1960s twin with two small engines and retractable wheels.

T6.name: North American T-6 Texan
T6.fact: A World War II trainer. Thousands of pilots learned to fly in one.

FA7X.name: Dassault Falcon 7X
FA7X.fact: A three-engine French business jet that can cross an ocean nonstop.
